text:
jessica: heads-up — we're getting a cluster of 5xx/timeouts for hosted inference routes (multiple customers) starting ~2026-03-15T12:02:30Z. spike from baseline ~0.5% -> ~8% on /v1/generate and streaming endpoints. customers report long hangs then 502/504. :rotating_light:

raj: looking. i'm seeing a lot of Redis timeouts and 'connection reset' on prefix-cache-prod. gateway logs show 504 after internal cache wait. also seeing connection pool exhaustion on cache clients.

tyler: +1. cache-bot alerted earlier: 'prefix-cache-prod latency >200ms, connections 98%'. i'm pulling metrics.

cache-bot: [ALERT] prefix-cache-prod: redis-instance-3 failing health checks, rtt p95=410ms, tcp_retransmits rising.

olivia: any deploys around that time? i see a config roll earlier that increased worker batch size for runtime. could be increased cache pressure.

jessica: customer support tickets: #CS-11233, #CS-11235 complaining timeouts. leaving customer notes and asking for ETA.

raj: digging into redis logs. seeing repeated errors:
```
[2026-03-15 12:01:57] ERROR: Connection reset by peer - while executing GET prefix:abc123
[2026-03-15 12:02:14] WARNING: DELAYED_COMMAND - client output buffer exceeded
[2026-03-15 12:02:31] ERROR: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
```
this matches pool exhaustion and occasional OOM evictions.

tyler: running quick health checks:
```
redis-cli -h redis-3.prod.redwood.internal INFO memory
# Memory
used_memory:123456789
maxmemory:125000000
used_memory_rss:130000000
```
looks like memory spikes close to maxmemory and then evictions. also seeing a lot of long-running zpop/zrange ops from prefix eviction code.

olivia: can we short-circuit prefix caching for hosted routes temporarily? we have a feature flag 'prefix_cache.enabled' per-tenant. toggling that off should force fallback to direct model KV or compute, avoiding Redis.

tyler: i'm going to flip the flag for affected routes + all prod tenants as a mitigation. will do canary first.

jessica: please post status updates so i can tell customers.

(5m later)

tyler: canary toggle done for 10% traffic -> successful. error rate on canary dropped to baseline. rolling to 100% now.

cache-bot: [INFO] prefix_cache feature-flag disabled for incoming-hosted routes.

raj: after toggling, cache request volume dropped ~85%, redis-3 memory pressure decreased, connection resets stopped. gateway 5xx dropped back to ~0.6% within ~7m.

jessica: reported back to customers: mitigating action taken, expected recovery. awaiting root cause analysis. :white_check_mark:

olivia: next steps: 1) scale redis cluster (add replica/reshard) 2) investigate what caused mem pressure: was it a change in data shape (longer prefixes) or a bug in eviction logic 3) add better backpressure: client-side circuit-breaker for cache timeouts 4) add more aggressive metrics/alerting for prefix hit ratio and memory headroom.

tyler: i've already spun up two additional cache nodes in the autoscale group and applied a temporary raising of maxmemory by +10% (within safety bounds). will monitor.

raj: adding more diagnostics: enabling slowlog and sampling of heavy keys. also suspect a bad ttl causing items to pile up. collecting keys with biggest size.

jessica: can we get an ETA for full restore and action item owners so i can update customers?

raj: ETA for stable cluster capacity: ~30-45m to rebalance replicas and validate. deep root-cause analysis will take a few hours; i'll own the RCA.

tyler: infra action items: scale nodes (done), run redis-cluster reshard tonight 01:00 UTC, add client-side pool size limits and backoff. i'll own infra tasks.

olivia: runtime/action items: add feature-flag fallback logic to bypass prefix cache on timeouts, add diagnostic headers to responses indicating cache fallback reason, create rollout to adjust batch size defaults. i'll own runtime tasks.

jessica: support/comms: i'll post incident note to status.redwood.com and send targeted emails to affected customers. i'll keep the thread updated.

(30m later)

raj: follow-up: redis slowlog shows heavy RPUSH calls from a background job that accidentally started in multiple replicas after a deploy — duplicate job instance writing large lists without TTL. that filled memory.

tyler: confirmed background job was misconfigured in the deploy that rolled at 12:00 — job concurrency env var defaulted to 5 instead of 1. rolling back that change fixed the duplicate writers.

olivia: marking incident mitigated. next: postmortem and prevention items (job semaphore, TTL enforcement, stronger canary for deploys that touch background workers).

jessica: thanks all — i'll draft the customer-facing summary and link the internal postmortem when ready. closing support escalations for now.

cache-bot: [RESOLVED] prefix-cache-prod redis-3 latency normalized.

---
actions_summary:
- Mitigation: disabled prefix_cache feature flag for hosted routes -> 5xx/timeouts dropped.
- Short-term infra: scaled cache nodes + raised maxmemory.
- Root cause: duplicate background job writing large lists -> memory exhaustion in Redis.
- Owners: raj (RCA), tyler (infra changes), olivia (runtime fallbacks/flags), jessica (customer comms).

please link this thread to incident tracker #INC-2026-047 and postmortem ticket PM-2026-112.
